newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up on good dlr supply, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up on good dlr supply, poor demand.

text.p: Fresh supply and poor demand for dollars combined with comments on the rupee by the chairman of India's leading commercial bank helped the Indian currency to end up against the dollar on Monday, dealers said.
The dollar closed at 35.88/90 against the dollar compared with Monday's opening level of 35.92/93, dealers said.
Usually on Mondays there is a spurt in dollar supply from expatriate Indians based in the Middle East, dealers said.
The intensity of dollar demand seen last week, mainly emanating from an influential Calcutta bank, was not there on Monday.
"They were not bidding high today," said a bank dealer.
Remarks by Pandurang Kakodkar, chairman of State Bank of India (SBI), the leading commercial bank, also affected the market's sentiment, dealers said.
Kakodkar, whose bank is a major player in the inter-bank foreign exchange market, told Reuters in an interview he expected the rupee would remain stable in the near term.
He said the rupee was not under pressure as Indian imports are not increasing.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) continued to buy spot August dollars, putting pressure on the forward premia.
The six-month annualised premium closed at 6.63 percent compared with the previous close of 6.79 percent.

Some bankers who hoped the rupee's fall to 35.98 last week from 35.88/89 level would be a prelude to a sharper correction of the rupee necessitated by the rupee's recent gains against leading currencies, were disappointed.
Some dealers are now hoping the federal budget, due on February 28, would trigger fresh movement in the exchange rate.
